result_text:
`all_files.zip` now looks up and names its entries from the configured aspect names, the same way the loose `aspect_<name>.txt` files are written. I haven't run the renamed-aspect case end to end, so that part is checked by reading the code only.

**What changed:** in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, the five hardcoded `aspect_*.txt` literals in the `all_files.zip` call are replaced by `getAspectFileListZipEntry(...)` calls for the main, test, generated, build-and-deploy and other aspects. The new private helper uses `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same function that names the loose files, and reads that file from the text folder. The entry order is unchanged.

**Why the export broke:** the literal `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` read threw once the file was named `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`. That exception skipped the rest of the `try` block, so `all_files.zip` and `git-history.zip` were never written, and the stack trace was the only sign.

**Verification:** `mvn -q -o -pl reports test` ran with no errors. There is no test covering the export, and I did not run an analysis with a renamed aspect. With the default configuration the entries should still come out as before.

Nothing is committed.
